issues.problem: The identifying paths list contains two identical entries (messages→channels→channel_members via messages.channel_id/channel_members.channel_id), seemingly duplicating the focal and auxiliary path descriptions without distinguishing the Sophie-membership filter from the agent-membership filter.
issues.repair: Either merge into a single path entry or add a distinguishing note (e.g., filter target) so the two membership-check joins are not presented as literal duplicates.

rationale: The compiled selector (messages→channels→channel_members, filtering channels.is_dm=true, channel_members.user_id='U_SOPHIE', messages.message_text contains 'circuit-tracer', with an auxiliary check for channel_members.user_id='U01AGENBOT9') correctly and uniquely isolates 1706100000.000001: among all messages containing 'circuit-tracer' (this one, 1706110000.000100, 1706112500.000001), only this one sits in a is_dm=true channel with Sophie as a member, matching the single-mode resolution. The three added negatives are well-motivated and correctly seeded: the wrong-partner DM message (1706100500.000001, D02AGENTPRIYA) fails the Sophie-membership condition, backed by newly inserted channel D02AGENTPRIYA and its two channel_members rows; the same-DM-different-topic message (1706100800.000001) shares the correct DM and membership but fails the content filter; and the public #engineering message (1706110000.000100, already in base seed) fails the is_dm condition, now explicitly supported by the added negative_public_channel and negative_public_channel_members roles/bindings. Written_attributes correctly omit the authentication-supplied user_id (fixed from the prior turn) and retain only message_text, parent_id, and channel_id as legitimate written/referent fields. The access_plan uses only documented Slack-replica API operations (users.conversations, conversations.members, conversations.history, chat.postMessage with thread_ts) without inventing unsupported capabilities. Mechanical checks report no errors and computed_matches/negatives align with the design intent. The only defect found is a cosmetic duplication in the cards' Identifying paths field, which does not affect correctness of the selection logic.
